codeVsHuman.method: Code built and tests passing is the share of the Built and Automated tests checks that passed. The separate Human testing done figure is the share of Real device, Real-world check and Ready to call Available that passed. It includes AI tests on real devices; it does not mean a person checked every feature. The final Ready check needs a human look, recorded by Nick. These separate figures keep their existing checklist method. Group figures are the average of their features and are never rounded up to 100. A feature shows "Code 100%" only when both of those code checks passed and no CODE item is still open; it counts as "Confirmed working on real devices" only when all five checks passed. Remaining counts are open road-to-100 items. All 70 features are counted, including those that are planned or on hold.

howToRead: Each feature has five checks. Built is worth 24 points. Passing automated tests adds 25. Running on a real phone or PC adds 25. The real-world check adds 25. Our test process uses AI testers on real devices for that check. At 99%, all four checks have passed and no known error is open. That means tested and confirmed working within the recorded checks. The feature is considered fully coded and working. The last 1% is a human look, not more building. Nick or a tester looks with their own eyes and says Ready. Only Nick records the Ready check. An open known error caps the score at 90%. Existing record limits can keep it lower. At 99%, the label is "Tested and working, waiting for a human look". At 100%, it is "Ready, a human confirmed". Each row says what was proven, when it was tested and what remains unverified. Each feature also has a road-to-100 list: what 100% means, what is done, and what remains, grouped as CODE (we can build or fix it), DEVICE (needs a real phone, PC, TV or car), NICK (his decision, account, money or legal) and BLOCKED.

All phones were muted, so nobody heard sound on a phone.

historyNew.headline: Published Android 1.51-tester23 on four phones, plus a three-phone Campsite test: no crash logged, three failures written down, no percentage changed

The home computers ran the Beebo desktop app: 0.1.87 for the morning S9+ run, 0.1.88 for the S24 run. An old Android 4.4 phone cannot run the app (it needs Android 7 or newer). Nick Will (owner) was present and watching live during the S24 and S25 runs, per his statement (from about 8:35 PM Eastern; the S9+, Pixel 3 and Campsite runs had no one watching).
historyNew.happened: Galaxy S9+: 47 passed, 3 failed, 2 need a newer desktop, 12 skipped. Pixel 3: 13 passed, 0 failed, 2 skipped. Galaxy S24 Ultra: 15 passed, 0 failed, 1 partly, 2 skipped. Galaxy S25: 14 passed, 0 failed. Campsite on three phones: 7 passed, 1 partly, 1 skipped. No crash was logged on any phone. Passed on the published file: the five tabs, the Back button rule on the screens tried, the Music header with no overlap, search with an ampersand, playing, pausing and seeking, Story mode (opening it and Back), Photos & backups (opening), the Connection route screen, away from home on 5G directly, one film forced through Beebo Relay, the Trip Journal video on the S24 Ultra and Pixel 3, Campsite host start and stop, guest pages, and Reversi between two guest phones. Failed: Trip Journal “Save as a video” on the Galaxy S9+ (muxing timeout, at 1080p, 720p and cards-only); the demo mode page says to tap a subtitles button the demo player does not have; Large playback controls looked the same size as off (low confidence). historyNew.headline: Full device pass: two Samsung phones, a Windows PC and a real Chromecast; three failures found, several fixes written but not yet published
historyNew.tested: A full device pass on Oct 13, 2026, about 7:00 AM to 1:15 PM Eastern, by a helper driving the devices with the owner nearby: a Samsung Galaxy S24 Ultra, a Samsung Galaxy S9+ (Android 10), the Windows dev PC, a home computer running the published desktop 0.1.87, and a real Chromecast on the Living Room TV, on home Wi-Fi and on 5G mobile data. Builds: the published downloads are Windows 0.1.87 and Android 1.51-tester22 (build 72). The phones ran a test build of the current code made that morning (tester22 plus some unmerged fixes; the app still shows 1.51-tester22) and the PC ran the unpublished 0.1.88 test build, so none of this counts as a test of a published download. An earlier same-morning two-phone Campsite and phone-speakers test, and a Sea Battle game played by two people, are included in the rows.
historyNew.happened: Passed on real devices: all five phone tabs on both phones; films (resume, play, pause, skip, quality menu, floating player on the S9+, 2x speed); a film on 5G through the direct route and through Beebo Relay (the relay first had to be switched on for the test account on the server, which the owner did); Watch Together on two phones (host, viewer, sync after a 45-second skip, leave and rejoin); a Car Party host and a passenger page on a second phone; Campsite hosting, a blank-name guest named "Guest 1", a guest reconnecting after 15 seconds offline, and 42 of 42 games opening (41 starting with a computer opponent; Crazy Eights played by hand); Chromecast with a person watching the TV (picture, sound, pause, play, skip both ways, a quality change and stop); radio and a podcast playing; a computer-made audiobook with chapters, jumps and speeds; sample music on both phones; playlists, watchlist, collections, Library health, Family Dashboard, Camp Jobs, a Packing List synced between two phones, Family Recipes; accessibility switches including Caregiver view; six languages on a phone and Spanish on the PC; the offline demo; the Share the app QR scan, download and install on the S9+; a trip link that opened on 5G with a photo and a clip once the away-from-home setting was on; all 27 Windows pages, five Home layouts, Customize layout, the update check and the signed-in browser player (17 of 17 pages, 720p/480p switching); phone speakers on two phones as a stereo pair. Failed: following a new podcast ("Your Beebo computer had a problem", three tries); the Trip Journal "Save as a video" (failed twice on the test build; with a fix on a branch it worked on the S24 for a 1-card and a 13-second trip, but the videos were not played back); the desktop Music window stayed silent at 0:00 (cause found and a fix written, not merged or re-tested in the real window); the ordinary trip link served from the home computer did not open from outside the home on 5G because the router did not let it in. Found, still open: the sound stops with the screen off by default (the Screen off: On option keeps it playing); the Music screen's Albums/Artists/Songs buttons overlap the "Mixes and radio" heading on both phones; a shared downloaded video was silent on a guest phone; the demo player has no subtitles button although its page says it does; phone volume buttons do not control the TV volume while casting; the live Car Party page still refuses a blank nickname (the automatic name is fixed in the code but not on the server); phone-speaker pages show a false Bluetooth warning and the PC speaker seat did not play in the surround test; no screen lets a customer switch Beebo Relay on for their own account. Not tested: Beebo Auto in a car, Android TV, Fire TV, TalkBack, a real wake of a sleeping PC, Live TV with a tuner, Chromecast to other TVs, converted films while casting, a first install from the QR on a phone that never had Beebo, accepting a library share, Walkie-talkie from anywhere, a real TV pairing code, Remote Desktop, Jellyfin, parental rules, an update installed over an older version, subtitles, and the new fixes on real devices. Ready to call Available was not ticked for any row, because the exact published downloads were not the ones tested.

historyNew.headline: Two-home real-device test: phone on 5G, home Wi-Fi and a friend’s Wi-Fi; relay, two viewers, library sharing, Windows hand test
historyNew.tested: A two-home test on Oct 12, 2026: a Windows PC at each of two separate homes on two different networks, one family server at a third home, a Samsung Galaxy S24 Ultra on home Wi-Fi, on 5G mobile data and at a friend’s Wi-Fi, a Galaxy S9+, and a browser on the S24 and on a PC. Builds: the published Android 1.51-tester22 (build 72), Windows desktop 0.1.87 (published) and a 0.1.88 test build that is not published.
historyNew.happened: Passed on real devices: away-from-home playback (a direct connection to a home PC worked; a connection through Beebo Relay worked from a phone on 5G once switched on, with the first picture in about 3 seconds; the phone browser on 5G also played); play, pause, resume (a 63-second pause held its exact position), seek and quality switching to 480p in the phone browser and in the phone app; two viewers watching at once from one home PC, both connected directly in about a second; the phone app kept playing across Wi-Fi to 5G to Wi-Fi switches and through 24 seconds of airplane mode; sharing a library with another home (send an invite, accept, play, and “stop sharing” refusing new playback within about 30 seconds); the online games lobby loaded; uploading from the phone to the home PC (Space Saver backup: 3 files arrived); browse sort and filters, favourites and watchlist, playlists, radio, podcasts, Campsite game-room coverage using scripted guests (not a hand-played result for another game), dark theme, landscape and restart. On this website, 67 of 67 home-page links returned OK, and the installer and APK sizes matched the update feeds. Windows hand test on the 0.1.88 test build: about 35 screens were opened and looked right (Home, Movies, TV Shows, Trailers, Discover, Live TV, Audiobooks, Podcasts, Radio, Music, Photos, Upload, Switch to Beebo, the admin pages, Users, Watch History, Story Studio and all eight Settings pages). Not yet done: Log out on screen, the signed-in browser player, subtitles and keyboard-only use. Found, fix written and tested in the code, not yet in a published download: a shared-library guest could be dropped to a sign-in screen with no way back to their own home; a stopped share showed a wrong message and still looked active in the guest’s list; the web player froze for minutes after a phone switched from Wi-Fi to mobile data; the home PC could stop accepting viewers after many sessions because ports were not released; the app’s own picture-in-picture window did not close properly; some text was clipped at 150% text size; Library health showed a misleading counter and a stale “cannot be reached” line; skip-intro jumped over a 2:39 opening scene on one show; Auto quality chose 480p on a fast home connection; a share with downloads switched off still offered a download button. Found, still open: a 40 to 70 second freeze after seeking far into a long converted film (a safeguard is written, but the cause is not fully confirmed); voices slightly out of sync after jumps on one TV episode (a likely cause was found and fixed in the code, but it is not confirmed on the real episode); the Read It To Me buttons were hidden behind the bottom bar (a fix is in progress); a new home name could not get its secure certificate until it was registered by hand; casting from a browser to a friend’s Chromecast was blocked because that TV is not yet registered for Beebo’s test receiver (casting to a TV through the phone app was proven earlier on the home TV). Not tested: Chromecast to the friend’s TV, Beebo Auto in a car, Watch Together with a second device, a real TV pairing code (Link a TV is switched off on the server; a wrong code was refused with a plain message), TalkBack, two people on Beebo Relay at once, the Windows Log out button on screen, a House-to-House share started from a PC, and the new fixes on real devices.

checkDefinitions.Built: The code exists and works in the build.
checkDefinitions.Automated tests: The test suite for it passes.
checkDefinitions.Real device: We ran it on a real phone, PC or TV and it worked.
checkDefinitions.Real-world check: Our test process uses AI testers on real devices in a realistic situation, such as away from home, in a car, on a real TV or with several devices. The dated evidence in each row records what was actually tried.
checkDefinitions.Ready to call Available: Nick or a tester has looked with their own eyes and said Ready. Only Nick records this check. It is worth the last 1 point: a human look, not more building.

ownerTestsNote: When Nick tests something himself, it is recorded here with the date, the device and the result; a check is only ticked if it passed.
ownerTestsSchema: features[].ownerTests is a list of {date ("Oct 20, 2026, 3:00 PM Eastern"), device, did, result ("PASS" or "FAIL"), notes, ticks (only on PASS; any of Real device, Real-world check, Ready to call Available)}. A Real device, Real-world check or Ready to call Available tick that is not in checksBaseline must be backed by a PASS ownerTests entry that lists it. Add entries with tools/the test record, never by editing checks by hand.
deviceTestsSchema: features[].deviceTests is a list of {tester, device, build, date ("Oct 19, 2026, 9:23 AM Eastern"), result ("PASS", "PARTIAL" or "FAIL"), evidence, ticks}. It records a test a helper ran on a real device. ticks may only be ["Real device"], only on a PASS, and only if every single-phone device item listed for the feature passed. A Real device tick after Oct 19, 2026 needs a PASS deviceTests or ownerTests record that lists it. Real-world check and Ready to call Available can only be ticked through ownerTests.

scoring.waitingLabel: Tested and working, waiting for a human look
scoring.rule: percentComplete is worked out from features[].checks and features[].openIssues by site-data/progress-score.js: Built 24, Automated tests 25, Real device 25, Real-world check 25, Ready to call Available 1 (only Nick records it). The first four add up to 99. A feature reaches 99 only when all four are true and openIssues is 0 (omitted means 0). An open known error caps the score at 90. An optional percentCap, explained by scoreNote, is a further limit. Check with: node site-data/check-progress-score.js.
scoring.explanation: Each feature has five checks. Built is worth 24 points. Passing automated tests adds 25. Running on a real phone or PC adds 25. The real-world check adds 25. Our test process uses AI testers on real devices for that check. At 99%, all four checks have passed and no known error is open. That means tested and confirmed working within the recorded checks. The feature is considered fully coded and working. The last 1% is a human look, not more building. Nick or a tester looks with their own eyes and says Ready. Only Nick records the Ready check. An open known error caps the score at 90%. Existing record limits can keep it lower. At 99%, the label is "Tested and working, waiting for a human look". At 100%, it is "Ready, a human confirmed". Each row says what was proven, when it was tested and what remains unverified.
